primary_diagnosis_treated: Diabetic nephropathy (type 2 diabetes mellitus driven chronic kidney disease) – CKD stage 4
nice_guideline_used: NICE NG203 (Chronic kidney disease: assessment and management) and NICE TA775 (SGLT2 inhibitors for CKD)

medications.dose: 1.25 mg orally once daily, titrate by doubling every 2–4 weeks to target 10 mg once daily as tolerated
medications.duration: Lifelong — review annually and after each dose change (1–2 weeks post‑dose for labs)
medications.purpose: Reduce proteinuria and slow CKD progression; control hypertension
medications.nice_justification: NG203 first‑line ACE‑I/ARB for CKD with ACR ≥30 mg/mmol or hypertension

medications.duration: Lifelong — review annually and monitor renal function
medications.purpose: Slows CKD progression and provides cardiovascular protection in eGFR 20–45 mL/min/1.73 m²
medications.nice_justification: TA775 recommends dapagliflozin 10 mg for CKD with eGFR 20‑45 mL/min/1.73 m², irrespective of diabetes status

medications.duration: Lifelong — review annually; increase to 40 mg if LDL‑C target not met
medications.purpose: Cardiovascular risk reduction; CKD is a CV‑risk equivalent
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends statin for all CKD patients for CV risk reduction

medications.duration: Lifelong — review annually; add only if BP remains >130/80 mmHg after ACE‑I titration
medications.purpose: Adjunct antihypertensive to achieve target <130/80 mmHg in heavy proteinuria
medications.nice_justification: NG203 non‑pharmacological BP target <130/80 mmHg when ACR ≥70 mg/mmol; amlodipine is a recommended add‑on

contraindications.reason: Accelerate CKD progression and cause fluid retention; contraindicated in eGFR 29 mL/min/1.73 m²
eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m² – risk of lactic acidosis
contraindications.alternative: Discontinue; consider dose reduction only if eGFR 30‑45 (not applicable here)

contraindications.reason: Increased risk of hyperkalaemia and acute kidney injury; NICE NG203 advises against dual RAAS blockade
contraindications.alternative: Use either an ACE‑I (ramipril) or an ARB, not both

contraindications.reason: High risk of contrast‑induced nephropathy with eGFR <30
contraindications.alternative: If imaging required, use prophylactic hydration and nephrology input

assumptions_warnings: Current blood pressure reading not provided – assume >130/80 mmHg pending titration of ramipril.
Serum potassium, liver function tests, and lipid profile not available – baseline labs required before initiating ramipril, atorvastatin, and dapagliflozin.
Allergy status unknown – verify no ACE‑I, statin, or SGLT2‑i hypersensitivity before prescribing.
HbA1c and diabetes medication list not provided – ensure no concurrent sulfonylureas/insulin that may increase hypoglycaemia risk with dapagliflozin.
Patient’s heart failure status not documented – avoid verapamil/diltiazem; amlodipine is acceptable if no severe HFrEF.
treatment_summary: Initiate renin‑angiotensin blockade with ramipril, add dapagliflozin for renal protection, start atorvastatin for cardiovascular risk, and consider amlodipine if blood pressure remains above target. Avoid NSAIDs, metformin, and dual ACE‑I/ARB therapy. Baseline labs and regular monitoring of eGFR, potassium, liver enzymes, and lipids are required per NICE NG203 and TA775.
